summary.text: A previously healthy 53-year-old man who formerly smoked two packs a day was admitted with exertional dyspnea and left shoulder pain for eight weeks. Chest CT showed a 36 mm left S3 mass, and bronchoscopy led to a diagnosis of squamous cell non-small cell lung cancer, cT2aN2M0, cStage IIIA.

He received first-line weekly carboplatin and paclitaxel with 60 Gy radiation, then 14 cycles of durvalumab, and the third line was changed to docetaxel after progressive disease. PET/CT and a left subclavian lymph node biopsy showed squamous cell carcinoma metastasis. He was hospitalized for fourth-line chemotherapy; chest X-ray and CT showed a massive pleural effusion, and blood and pleural fluid tests were reported.

On the night of the hospitalization day for fourth-line chemotherapy, vesicular exanthema appeared on the left lateral chest. Valaciclovir was given for suspected herpes zoster, the rash worsened three days later and reached the right wrist, and a positive Tzanck smear led to a diagnosis of generalized herpes zoster. Intravenous aciclovir was started and withdrawn eight days later after improvement, and he was discharged.

Two weeks later he was rehospitalized, and a 3 mm subcutaneous nodule in the left sternal clavicle was biopsied, showing cutaneous metastasis of squamous cell carcinoma; it was surgically removed because of pain. About three weeks later, during fourth-line chemotherapy, he died of respiratory failure due to progressive lung cancer and massive pleural effusion.
